title: Day 28 · Week 4, Day 0 — Body: smaller than a grain of salt — what the embryo is on the day the test turns positive
summary: The first numbered episode: the missed period and the positive test. What your baby physically is today — a two-layered disc about 0.2 mm across (Carnegie stage 5–6) inside a ~2 mm package that has already buried into the uterine wall and begun building a placenta — and the primitive streak that is about to fix head, tail, left and right. Why the test is positive now: hCG from the trophoblast, implantation on day 8–10 after ovulation in 84% of lasting pregnancies, a median 124% rise every two days, and the real sensitivity of home tests (97% vs 54–67% detection on the day of the missed period). The due-date math from ACOG Committee Opinion 700 — 280 days by convention, half of women misrecall their LMP, the ±5–7-day crown-rump accuracy and the redating thresholds — and the Jukic 2013 finding that healthy pregnancies with known conception dates vary by 37 days. The honest early-loss curve (25% of hormone-detected conceptions before 6 weeks; 10% at age 25–29 rising to 53% at 45+), the ectopic warning signs that justify a same-day call, what the first phone call to the OB should accomplish and why the first visit is at 8–12 weeks, folic acid and alcohol today, and the established answer on the trip that is already booked.
action: One phone call: book the first OB or midwife visit, with your partner or on her behalf. Ask how to reach the practice after hours between now and then, and save that number in both phones under a name you will find at 3 a.m. If she is not on a prenatal vitamin with at least 400 µg folic acid, pick one up on the way home.
